wa_northwest_arete.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
wa_northwest_arete.note: Self-issue day-use wilderness permit at the kiosk; parking is very limited and the Enchantment Permit Area prohibits dogs.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Argonaut Peak summit (west summit, true)
wa_northwest_arete.note: True summit is the west of two nearly equal summits (SE and W); most parties reverse the arete with short rappels through the crux, then downclimb the couloir.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Colchuck Lake / Stuart Lake trail fork
wa_northwest_arete.note: Trail flattens at a signed fork — Colchuck Lake left, Stuart Lake right; take the Colchuck side toward Mountaineer Creek.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Cross-country departure into Mountaineer Creek drainage
wa_northwest_arete.note: Leave the maintained trail here for brushy, off-trail travel through Devil's Club, slide alder, and boulder-strewn creek terrain toward Argonaut's north side.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Lower basin below Argonaut's north face
wa_northwest_arete.note: Rough rest/bivy basin where the bushwhack ends and the technical approach up the granite slab begins.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Snow-covered granite slab
wa_northwest_arete.note: Steep, partly snow-covered granite slab leading into the couloir; slick and exposed when wet or icy.

wa_northwest_arete.name: 40+ degree snow/ice couloir
wa_northwest_arete.note: Couloir steepens to 40+ degrees near its top; crampons recommended for the final pitch to the notch.

wa_northwest_arete.name: Notch below the Northwest Arete
wa_northwest_arete.note: Gain the ridge here and rope up for roughly seven pitches of Class 4 to 5.6+ climbing up the arete.

wa_south_face_12.name: Beverly Turnpike Trailhead
wa_south_face_12.note: Shared trailhead with Bean Creek Basin at the end of the rough, overgrown FR 9737-112 spur road.

wa_south_face_12.name: Argonaut Peak summit (west summit, true)
wa_south_face_12.note: Final moves onto the true (west) summit ridge are harder than the class 2 approach suggests, often low class 3/4.

wa_south_face_12.name: Beverly Creek Trail (FST 1391) / Fourth Creek Trail (FST 1226.1) junction
wa_south_face_12.note: Faint fork in forested/open terrain; bear toward Fourth Creek Trail for the pass rather than continuing up Beverly Creek.

wa_south_face_12.name: Fourth Creek Pass
wa_south_face_12.note: Low, treed pass on the drainage divide reached via a steep final 0.3-mile push; descends into the Fourth Creek drainage on the far side.

wa_south_face_12.name: Fourth Creek / Ingalls Creek confluence camp
wa_south_face_12.note: Established basecamp near the creek confluence used by most south-side parties before the summit push.

wa_south_face_12.name: Ingalls Creek ford
wa_south_face_12.note: Potentially dangerous ford — cold and swift in early season, can be partially frozen with slick ice-covered rocks.

wa_south_face_12.name: South-side gully, west of the main gully
wa_south_face_12.note: Class 2 scrambling up loose rock in the gully just west of Argonaut's main south gully, heading for the summit ridge.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (Trail 674)
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: End of FS-32 (Hannegan Pass Road) off Mt. Baker Highway; Northwest Forest Pass required at the kiosk, and this is the start of the long multi-day approach toward Bear Creek.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Bear Mountain summit
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: True summit horn gained via seven pitches of 5.10 climbing up the buttress above the couloir; descend west/south on the standard route with downclimbing and short rappels back toward the saddle camp.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Hannegan Pass
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: Broad meadow saddle where Hannegan Pass Trail meets the Chilliwack River Trail; leave the maintained tread here and drop north into the Chilliwack River valley toward Canada.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Bear Creek Camp (Chilliwack River Trail)
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: Established camp at the Bear Creek confluence on the Chilliwack River Trail, the jump-off point for the Bear Mountain approach; NPS closed this camp after the 2021 Bear Creek Fire, so verify current access before counting on it.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Meadows above Ruta Lake
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: From Bear Creek, climb steep timber then huckleberry slopes east to treeline; the route gains the divide crest in open meadowland just above Ruta Lake.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: NW Ridge saddle high camp (6,480')
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: Traverse loose south-facing slopes below Points 6592 and 6822, crossing a rock rib, to this saddle on Bear's NW ridge — the standard bivy for the North Buttress, roughly 9 hours from the trailhead.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.name: Glacier couloir base below North Buttress
wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.note: About 1.5 hours below camp; loose rock and occasional icefall/rockfall off the shrinking glacier remnant in the couloir make early starts and helmets essential here.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Small unmarked pullout at roughly mile 22 of Cascade River Road across from Johannesburg Mountain; room for only 6-8 cars and no facilities.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Boston Peak
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: True summit; final ridge is extremely loose, friable rock (5.5 X) with serious exposure, and the FA party simply continued their traverse rather than downclimbing, so a separate descent must be planned.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Old miner's cabin site (Boston Basin mine relic)
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Remains of a historic mining cabin mark the trail breaking out of forest onto the open basin slopes; steep, eroded tread up to this point.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: South Fork Boston Creek crossing
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Last easy, reliable creek crossing just below the lower Boston Basin camps; fill up here before heading into the alpine.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Lower Boston Basin Camp
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Established backcountry campsites just above treeline; NPS wilderness permit required and food must be stored per park regulations.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Western edge of Quien Sabe Glacier
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Climbers leave the upper basin meadows/moraine here and rope up for glacier travel toward Sharkfin Col.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Quien Sabe Glacier crevasses / Sharkfin bergschrund
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Large crevasses open on this glacier by late season and a substantial bergschrund forms beneath the couloir below Sharkfin Tower; probe or find a snow bridge.

wa_northwest_ridge_2.name: Sharkfin Col
wa_northwest_ridge_2.note: Low point on the ridge just west of Sharkfin Tower; the FA route gains the crest here via a loose, chossy couloir off Sharkfin before traversing onto Boston's northwest ridge.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: SR 20 / State Creek Pullout
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Same unsigned SR 20 pullout used for the South Buttress, ~1.5 mi west of Washington Pass (~0.5 mi west of the Blue Lake trailhead).

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: Cutthroat Peak summit
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Final low-5th-class pitch/scramble tops out on the blocky true summit; reverse the ridge with downclimbing and short rappels to descend.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: State Creek crossing
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Cross State Creek in the forest below the pullout before climbing into the meadows/basin southwest of the summit.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: Basin below Whistler Mountain
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Trail runs along the north side of the drainage and flattens through the open basin around 6200 ft before angling up toward Cutthroat's southwest side.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: Southwest Gully entrance
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Talus/scree/sand gully gaining the ridge; in poor visibility parties have mistaken this for the steeper, harder Second Southwest Gully just to the right.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: Crux face above rap station
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: A short 5.2 face above a double-bolt belay/rappel anchor leads to easy ledges below the ridge crest; rock is loose in spots.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: West Ridge crest / notch
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Gain the ridge crest here at a notch giving access toward the north ridge; narrow, exposed catwalk over a series of crestline horns.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: Northwest face traverse (Northwest Ledge)
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.note: Exposed, near-two-rope-length traverse across the northwest face on the ledge finish to reach the north ridge below the summit block.

wa_cutthroat_west_ridge.name: West Ridge base / area reference point

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Self-issue day-use wilderness permit and NW Forest Pass required at the kiosk; parking fills fast in this heavily-trafficked Enchantments quota area.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Colchuck Lake / Stuart Lake trail split
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Signed junction roughly 2-2.5 mi in; bear left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Colchuck Lake
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Established backcountry camps and reliable water near the outlet; dogs prohibited in the Enchantment Permit Area.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Lateral moraine crest (Colchuck Glacier)
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Boulder-hop the south/east shore then gain the moraine crest deposited by the Colchuck Glacier to avoid loose talus below the north face.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Hidden Couloir base
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Base of the north-face couloir system below the glacier's east lobe; check avalanche and icefall conditions before committing in winter/spring.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Mid-face ice runnels
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: Route narrows through runnels splitting the mid-face rock band; reported as thin, unpredictable ice depending on the season.

wa_dragontail_peak_r1.name: Dragontail Peak summit
wa_dragontail_peak_r1.note: True summit; descend the standard Aasgard Pass scramble route back to Colchuck Lake.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Self-issue day-use wilderness permit and NW Forest Pass required at the kiosk.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Colchuck Lake
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Reliable water and camps; skirt the shore toward the north face.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Lateral moraine crest
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Gain the Colchuck Glacier's moraine crest to reach the base of the north face.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Face low point / route start
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Snow ramps just right of the low point of the north face mark the start; graded WI3+ M4 in winter/spring mixed conditions.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Dark rock band runnels
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Route follows ice runnels splitting the band of dark rock two-thirds up the face — the technical crux, quality ice-dependent.

wa_dragontail_peak_r2.name: Dragontail Peak summit
wa_dragontail_peak_r2.note: Descend the standard Aasgard Pass scramble route.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: Self-issue day-use wilderness permit and NW Forest Pass required at the kiosk.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: Dragontail Peak summit
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: From the notch, drop down and traverse northeast to the true summit; descend via Aasgard Pass.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: Colchuck Lake
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: Reliable water and camps; head along the north shore toward the Colchuck Glacier.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: North shore / glacier approach
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: Ascend easy snow on the Colchuck Glacier's east lobe toward Colchuck Col.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: Colchuck Col
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: Saddle between Colchuck Peak and Dragontail; the couloir start is a couple hundred feet left (east) of the col.

wa_dragontail_peak_r3.name: Pandora's Box notch
wa_dragontail_peak_r3.note: Steep snow/ice couloir (up to roughly 35-40 degrees near the bottom) leading to a notch in the ridge; some parties rope up here.

wa_forbidden_peak_east_ridge.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_forbidden_peak_east_ridge.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road ~21.7 mi from Marblemount; NW Forest Pass to park, self-issue wilderness permit required.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road ~21.7 mi from Marblemount; NW Forest Pass to park, self-issue wilderness permit required.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Forbidden Peak
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: True summit; descend via the West Ridge couloir back to Boston Basin.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Boston Basin High Camp
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: Standard base camp for both Torment and Forbidden; continue northeast along the Quien Sabe Glacier's west edge toward Sharkfin Col.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Sharkfin Col
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: Low point on the ridge left of Sharkfin Tower, gained via ~10 ft of 5.7 rock and a 200-ft class-3 gully; loose scree underfoot.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Rappel to Boston Glacier
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: ~150-ft rappel down a loose gully off the col to reach the Boston Glacier; watch for rope-snag on loose rock.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: Boston Glacier crevasse traverse
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: Northward traverse through heavily crevassed terrain toward the north end of the glacier; a fall here would be serious, kick solid steps.

wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.name: North Ridge crest
wa_forbidden_peak_north_ridge.note: Ridge regained above a 5.6 left-facing corner crux; two small snow-free bivy spots sit just below on the northeast side.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road ~21.7 mi from Marblemount; NW Forest Pass to park, self-issue wilderness permit required.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Forbidden Peak
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: True summit; descend the West Ridge couloir into Boston Basin.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Boston Basin High Camp
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: Base camp on flats below the glaciers; from here work northeast across glaciated terrain toward the peak's northeast side.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Glacier approach below NE face
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: Rope travel across the glacial basin toward the base of the northeast face, staying alert for hidden crevasses.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Bergschrund crossing
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: Cross the bergschrund guarding the base of the face; widens and can be tricky to negotiate by late spring.

wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.name: Northeast Face snow/ice climb
wa_forbidden_peak_northeast_face.note: Sustained firm snow and ice up to ~55 degrees with little protection; best climbed early season while still well frozen.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road ~21.7 mi from Marblemount; NW Forest Pass to park, self-issue wilderness permit required.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Forbidden Peak
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: True summit; descend the West Ridge couloir into Boston Basin.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Boston Basin High Camp
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: Base camp on flats below the Boston/Forbidden glaciers; head northwest across glaciated terrain toward the face.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Boston/Forbidden glacier basin
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: Rope up and cross the glacier basin toward the northwest aspect of the peak, weaving around moats and crevasses.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Moat/bergschrund at face base
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: Cross the moat/bergschrund at the base of the northwest face, stepping from ice onto rock; often the technical crux of the approach in late season.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Northwest Face ice band
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: ~900 ft of 30-45 degree snow and ice in two sections split by a narrow rock band; front-pointing likely by mid-summer.

wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.name: Knife-edge / North Ridge crest
wa_forbidden_peak_northwest_face.note: Steep, somewhat loose 4th-to-low-5th climbing leads to a knife-edge crossed at 5.6 (crux 5.8) where the route joins the upper North Ridge.

wa_forbidden_peak_west_ridge.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_forbidden_peak_west_ridge.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road ~21.7 mi from Marblemount; NW Forest Pass to park, self-issue wilderness permit required.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Snow Lake / Alpental Trailhead
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Large gravel lot off Alpental Rd (I-90 exit 52); Northwest Forest Pass required, unsigned West Face boot path leaves the Snow Lake Trail roughly 50 ft downhill from the trailhead.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Guye Peak summit
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: True summit (5,168 ft); small register, open views over Snoqualmie Pass and across to Cave Ridge and Snoqualmie Mountain.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Talus cone & rocky streambed below West Face
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Boot path climbs through slide alder onto an open talus cone, then a rising traverse crosses a rocky streambed (often dry) to the base of the face — helmet strongly advised, climber-kicked rockfall is common here.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Large tree-covered ramp
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Exit the streambed right onto a broad, rising ramp with full-grown trees that traverses the whole west face north to south; some parties belay this, most scramble it.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Notch at top of the ramp
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Ramp ends at a notch; pass through it to climber's right into a wide gully where the crux pitch begins.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Crux crack/face pitch
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Low 5th-class crack/face for ~30 ft easing to Class 4 through alpine trees for about half a rope length; belay just below the notch above.

wa_guye_peak_r1.name: Guye Peak–Cave Ridge saddle
wa_guye_peak_r1.note: Standard walk-off descent drops from the north/true summit down to this saddle before continuing north to rejoin the Snow Lake/Cave Ridge trail system back to Alpental.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Ross Dam Trailhead
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: SR 20 MP 134 pullout (4 cars + 2 ADA spots), just past the winter closure gate; no day-use fee, but a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Info Center is required to camp.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Luna Peak
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: From the Class 2-3 false summit, downclimb the exposed Class 4 chimney then traverse narrow ledges on the east face (running belay recommended) to the true summit.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Ross Dam / Ross Lake crossing
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Trail drops 0.8 mi to Ross Dam; cross the dam and either hike the Ross Lake shoreline or catch the seasonal water taxi (reserve through Ross Lake Resort) north to the Big Beaver Trailhead.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: 39 Mile Camp
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Small 3-site camp on Big Beaver Creek near a stand of ancient red cedars; water at the 39 Mile Creek crossing, no bear box so hang food carefully.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Luna Camp
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Last maintained-trail camp before leaving Big Beaver Trail; onward travel to Access Creek is off-trail bushwhacking.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Big Beaver Creek ford / Access Creek brush
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Waist-deep ford of Big Beaver Creek (a logjam crossing exists downstream) followed by dense alder-swath bushwhacking up the Access Creek drainage.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Access Creek Basin
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Boulder-strewn basin used as base camp, with a flat-top boulder as a common tent platform; last reliable water before the high traverse to Luna Pass.

wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Luna Pass
wa_luna_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Gains the Luna Cirque high country via the Access Couloir/Col; established tent sites 50 ft above the pass to the north mark the start of the southeast-slopes scramble.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Bridge Creek Trailhead
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: SR-20 milepost ~159, ~2 mi east of Rainy Pass; NPS backcountry permit required for overnight camping, $5/day USFS parking fee, no potable water on site.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Goode Mountain summit
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Highest point in North Cascades National Park; summit block above the notch adds exposed class 4-5 moves before the true top.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: PCT / North Fork Bridge Creek Trail junction
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Leave the Pacific Crest Trail here and turn onto the North Fork Bridge Creek Trail toward Goode's north side.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Grizzly Creek crossing
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Usually an easy log crossing but reported as a dangerously high, hard-to-find ford in early season; trail turns brushy/overgrown just beyond it.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Lateral moraine camp above Goode Glacier
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Established bivy atop the lateral moraine overlooking the Goode Glacier's seracs; standard base camp for the Southwest Couloir attempt.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Goode Glacier crossing
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Cross the glacier from the moraine camp to reach the couloir base; route-finding is tricky and late-season snow bridges can be deteriorated.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.name: Black Tooth Notch
wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.note: Foot-wide notch gained by an exposed class 4 traverse (fixed sling marks the crux step); rock here is loose/"garbage" — watch for rockfall onto climbers below.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Ross Dam Trailhead
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: SR 20 milepost 134 parking lot; Northwest Forest Pass required. Descend the Ross Dam Trail toward the lake to reach Ross Lake Resort and arrange a paid water-taxi pickup.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: West Fury (Mount Fury, West Peak)
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: True, officially-named summit of Mount Fury. Descend by reversing the ridge traverse to East Fury, then drop East Fury's east-side glacier/scree gully back to Luna Col.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Big Beaver Landing (water-taxi drop)
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: Ross Lake Resort's boat drops climbers here to skip miles of lakeshore trail; self-issue wilderness permit kiosk and start of the Big Beaver Creek Trail.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Luna Camp
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: Established backcountry camp on the maintained Big Beaver Creek Trail through old-growth forest, roughly 8 trail miles above Big Beaver Landing.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Access Creek crossing
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: About 1.5 miles past Luna Camp, leave the maintained trail and ford Big Beaver Creek to pick up the faint, cairned Access Creek climbers' path described in Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Access Creek headwaters basin
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: Cairned climbers' path up the north flank crosses to the creek's south bank near 3,700 ft where brush thickens, then continues to good camping at the basin below the Luna-McMillan col.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: Luna Col
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: Notch between Luna Peak and a small tower on the Luna-McMillan arm; a small snowfield at the saddle usually provides running water and there's a good camp spot here or ~150 ft below on the east side.

wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.name: East Fury (ridge traverse start)
wa_mount_fury_west_west_ridge.note: Higher of Fury's twin summits and the start of the ~5.4 YDS, Grade III ridge traverse over three towers to West Fury; loose, exposed rock — rope up for the gendarmes.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Lena Lake Trailhead
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: FS Road 25 trailhead on the Hamma Hamma River; well-graded Lena Lake Trail #810 starts here, Northwest Forest Pass required to park.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Mount Stone (South Summit)
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: Class 3 scramble on solid pillow basalt from St. Peter's Gate; in fog it's easy to confuse the true south summit with the nearby Middle and North summits, and the final gully narrows to Class 3-4.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Lena Lake
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: 55-acre lake with an established Forest Service campground on the west shore; last reliable, easy-access water before the climb steepens toward the upper basin.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Upper Lena Lake
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: Backcountry camp basin just inside Olympic National Park; wilderness permit and bear canister required, and the maintained tread effectively ends here as the Scout Lake way-trail continues off-trail.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Scout Pass
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: Primitive way-trail crosses this pass through huckleberry-heather meadows past Lena Tarn and Scout Lake; tread is faint and easy to lose in fog or fresh snow.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: St. Peter's Gate
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: Rocky notch in Mt. Stone's southeast ridge and the traverse's high point, reached via a steep snow/dirt ramp over loose glacial moraine above Ullin's Bathtubs; gap opens onto the Lake of the Angels basin beyond.

wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.name: Putvin Trail cliff/handline section
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse.note: Steep, eroded cliff band on the descent below Whitehorse Basin and the Pond of the False Prophet, rigged with a fixed handline and an exposed root system used as a ladder; greasy and dangerous when wet.

wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.name: Nooksack Cirque Trailhead
wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.note: End of FS Road 34 off Hannegan Pass Rd; shared trailhead with the Price Glacier route. Ruth Creek has no bridge here — cross on the logjam just downstream.

wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.name: Nooksack Tower summit
wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.note: Beckey-Schmidtke (1946 FA) tops out via ~1,200 ft of 4th-class (5.4 crux) climbing along the north arête. A subsidiary summit of the Shuksan massif, 0.75 mi NE of Shuksan's main summit.

wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.name: Price Creek crossing / leave Nooksack Cirque trail
wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.note: Leave the maintained tread here, cross the Nooksack on a log, and climb the steep flagged forest slope toward Price Lake.

wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.name: Price / East Nooksack Glacier bivy basin
wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.note: Flat bivy spot shared with Price Glacier approach parties; routes diverge from here toward Nooksack Tower's north face.

wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.name: North Face couloir / bergschrund
wa_mount_shuksan_beckey_schmidtke.note: Base of the technical climbing — a 50-70° snow/ice couloir (the FA's '800 ft. ice couloir'). Cross the bergschrund and climb to the rock trough above.

wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.name: White Salmon Glacier toe
wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.note: Glacier travel begins where the road/approach ends.

wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.name: Winnie's Slide
wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.note: 150-200 ft step of steep 40-45° snow/ice onto the Upper Curtis Glacier; schrund can be tricky late season.

wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.name: Hell's Highway
wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.note: Snow chute connecting to the west edge of the Sulphide Glacier.

wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels.name: Putvin Trailhead (Trail #813)
wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels.note: Same trailhead as the Putvin Trail route; unmarked pullout on Hamma Hamma River Rd (FR 25).

wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.name: Shannon Ridge TH
wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.note: End of FR 1152-014 spur off Baker Lake Road.

wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.name: Sulphide Glacier camp
wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.note: Camp at the pass where Shannon Ridge's flat crest meets the glacier.

wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.name: Notch below SE Ridge
wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.note: Trend right off the Sulphide Glacier onto the ridge; ~600 vertical ft of 5.3-5.7 to the summit.

wa_chockstone_route.name: Blue Lake TH
wa_chockstone_route.note: SR 20 pullout 1.5 mi west of Washington Pass.

wa_chockstone_route.name: Spire col (gully base)
wa_chockstone_route.note: Base of the gully between North and South Early Winters Spires, below the giant chockstones.

wa_chockstone_route.name: Chockstone crux
wa_chockstone_route.note: 5.7 pitch bypassing the first giant chockstone on the left.

wa_labor_pains.name: Chockstone Route start (shared)
wa_labor_pains.note: Shares its start with the Chockstone Route before breaking left onto steeper 5.11a terrain.

wa_the_west_face.name: Base of West Face
wa_the_west_face.note: Low-angle cracks lead to a tree-topped chimney on the left side of the west face; shares the start with the NW Corner.

wa_beckey_davis.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
wa_beckey_davis.note: Alternate access only, used when the standard Stuart Lake Trailhead / Aasgard Pass approach is closed (e.g. wildfire closures) -- longer route via Snow Lakes/Lake Viviane (~10 mi one-way, per this route's own approach text). Stuart Lake Trailhead is the standard/preferred access described in the approach field.

wa_beckey_davis.name: Prusik Peak
wa_beckey_davis.note: South Face route, 6-7 pitches, FA Beckey-Davis 1962.

wa_beckey_davis.name: Gnome Tarn
wa_beckey_davis.note: Landmark tarn on the boot path leading to the base of Prusik Peak's south face routes.

wa_boving_christensen.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
wa_boving_christensen.note: Icicle Creek Rd approach into the Enchantments (Alpine Lakes Wilderness); overnight permit required.

wa_energizer_bunny.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
wa_energizer_bunny.note: Icicle Creek Rd approach into the Enchantments (Alpine Lakes Wilderness); overnight permit required.

wa_energizer_bunny.name: Prusik Peak
wa_energizer_bunny.note: South Face, left of Solid Gold, joins it near the top; 4-5 pitches.

wa_stanley_burgner.name: "Stuart Lake Trailhead"
wa_stanley_burgner.note: Icicle Creek Rd approach into the Enchantments (Alpine Lakes Wilderness); overnight permit required.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Boston Basin Trailhead (Cascade River Road pullout)
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Unmarked pullout at mile ~22 of Cascade River Road opposite Johannesburg Mountain, room for 6-8 cars; self-issue wilderness permit and Northwest Forest Pass required.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Sahale Mountain summit
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Short, exposed 3rd/4th-class scramble up the summit block from the col; the true summit block has fixed anchors used by many parties to rappel back to the col.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Creek crossings through old-growth forest
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Climbers' path follows an old mining road then crosses several small streams in old-growth timber before switchbacking to treeline; reliable water but poorly marked in low light.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Boston Basin low camp
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Designated moraine campsite with composting toilet at treeline; most parties continue higher for a shorter summit day.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Boston Basin high camp
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Upper hardened camp on slabs/grass below Sharkfin Tower, closer to the Quien Sabe Glacier; on-file beta's 'informal camps below Sharkfin' correspond to this bench.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Glacier rope-up point beneath Sharkfin Tower
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Where the boot path meets continuous snow on the Quien Sabe Glacier's lower-angle (north/left) side; rope up for crevasses here.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Bergschrund crossing
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Narrow snow bridge crosses above and left of the bergschrund late-season; crevasses widen through August-September and the crossing point shifts year to year.

wa_sahale_mountain_r1.name: Boston-Sahale Col
wa_sahale_mountain_r1.note: Top of the glacier traverse beneath the Sharkfin face; gains the col between Sahale and Boston Peak before the final scramble.

wa_sherpa_peak_west_ridge.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (N Fork Teanaway River Rd)

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: SR-20 Burgundy Col pullout (MP 165)
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Roadside pullout on the North Cascades Highway, first pullout past the Cutthroat Creek trailhead turnout, ~4 mi east of Washington Pass; Northwest Forest Pass needed to park.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Silver Star Mountain (East Summit)
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: True summit is the east peak reached by a short 4th-class scramble off the saddle; Wine Spires ridge visible to the north.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Early Winters Creek crossing
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Drop down the embankment off the highway and cross on logs — last easy, reliable water until the Bench or Col trickles.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Larch bench camp ("the Bench")
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Flat larch-shaded bench reached via the climber's trail on the timbered rib left of Burgundy Creek; a seasonal trickle nearby dries up by late summer.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Burgundy Col
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Gain the col via the gully above the Bench, staying left; 3-4 exposed bivy sites here and the last snowmelt trickle before the glacier.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Steep snow drop onto glacier's north flank
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Downclimb steep snow off the col, rope up, and traverse below Burgundy Spire's loose rock slabs — rockfall and, late season, open crevasses.

wa_silver_star_glacier.name: Silver Star Glacier saddle
wa_silver_star_glacier.note: Top of the Silver Star Glacier at the saddle between the west and east summits; steepens noticeably in the last pitch, crampons/axe mandatory.

wa_diamond_in_the_rough.name: Bedal Creek/Sloan Creek Trailhead
wa_diamond_in_the_rough.note: End of FR-4096, ~3 mi off the Mountain Loop Highway south of Bedal Campground.

wa_diamond_in_the_rough.name: Sloan Peak Summit
wa_diamond_in_the_rough.note: Shared summit for Sloan Peak's technical routes.

wa_diamond_in_the_rough.name: Climber's trail junction (leaves Bedal Creek trail for the basin)
Route GPS pin (Mountain Project, SW Face)

wa_fire_on_the_mountain.name: Bedal Creek/Sloan Creek Trailhead
wa_fire_on_the_mountain.note: End of FR-4096, ~3 mi off the Mountain Loop Highway south of Bedal Campground.

wa_fire_on_the_mountain.name: Sloan Peak Summit
wa_fire_on_the_mountain.note: 7-pitch 5.10d route up the southwest face, topping out at the shared summit.

wa_fire_on_the_mountain.name: Climber's trail junction (leaves Bedal Creek trail for the basin)

wa_northwest_buttress.name: Bedal Creek/Sloan Creek Trailhead
wa_northwest_buttress.note: End of FR-4096, ~3 mi off the Mountain Loop Highway south of Bedal Campground.

wa_northwest_buttress.name: Sloan Peak Summit
wa_northwest_buttress.note: Longest route on the peak; shared summit with good bivy spots along the buttress.

wa_northwest_buttress.name: Climber's trail junction (leaves Bedal Creek trail for the basin)

wa_the_triad_east_peak.name: Hidden Lake Trailhead (FR-1540 / Sibley Creek Road)

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Niederprum Trailhead
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Park at the washed-out 2008 bridge on 387th Ave NE/Old Mine Road (steel gate and boulder barricade); the old Niederprum mining-road grade climbs south from here toward Snow Gulch.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Whitehorse Mountain summit
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: True summit, typically gained by a short roped pitch or snowfinger above the wind cirque; descent reverses the glacier and Lone Tree Pass snow slopes.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Creek-drainage bushwhack (~1,100-2,200 ft)
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Steep, brush-choked section of the drainage above the trailhead that's only reasonably passable once deep spring snow has buried the alder and devil's club.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Niederprum Mine bench / traverse start
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Sloping bench near the old Niederprum mine workings, marked by a large broken, silvered snag; begin the rising leftward traverse toward Lone Tree Pass here.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Lone Tree Pass
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Gain this narrow notch via a steep snowfield (crampons recommended) — the transition point from forested ridge to open alpine/glacier terrain.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Whitehorse Ridge Camp
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Broad snow platform just beyond Lone Tree Pass with room for several tents and views from Mt. Baker to Dome Peak; the standard high camp for a two-day ascent.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: High Pass
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: A broad snow couloir below prominent Point 6357 tops out here; this pass is the entry point onto the Whitehorse (So-Bahli-Ahli) Glacier.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.name: Whitehorse Glacier bergschrund / wind-cirque snowfinger
wa_whitehorse_mountain_r1.note: Crevasses and a bergschrund open across the upper glacier by mid-summer near the 'wind cirque' snowfinger below the summit block; rope up and probe snow bridges.
